subject: english
question:
Identify the option that rectifies the error in the given sentence.

In 2023, she will has been working in the company for three years.
solution:
The correct option is: **she will have been.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence aims to use the future perfect continuous tense which indicates an action that will continue up until a point in the future.
 
• The correct structure for the future perfect continuous tense is** "will have been" **+ **present participle (verb+ing).**

Therefore, the phrase **"will has been"** is incorrect and should be **"will have been"** to fit the tense requirement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **future perfect continuous tense **is used to express an ongoing action that will be completed at some specified future time.
 
• It is formed by using "**will have been" **followed by the present participle form of the verb, which ends **in -ing.**
 
• **"in 2023"** is not the error here; it correctly sets the future time reference.
 
• The preposition** "in"** in** "in the company" **is correctly used to indicate the place of employment.
